**CFTC and ETF Report** _A weekly update of futures and exchange traded fund activity._ 

- The complex traded bullish again after a major dip in all metals at the beginning of the month owing to uncertainty over the actions of the Greek government. Bullish US Auto figures helped pgms, and the cut in ECB rates, combined with the impression that QEIII was on the slipway and being given a fresh coat of paint, added to the positive gold outlook. 

- Investor interest grew on the long side for gold by 1.40 million tozs on COMEX.  Platinum saw decent NYMEX buying, but that was largely offset by selling from TOCOM as the drop in the Yen gave Japanese investors a chance to take some profit on Platinum. Palladium saw a 3 % rise in investor longs overall. 

- ETF holdings grew for gold, silver and platinum, but went sideways for palladium in the week to the 28th of October.

- Gold has had a positive week with a dip to the lows on December COMEX of $1681 being ferociously bid back up during the 1st of November and a close of

$1756.10 on Friday. If gold couldn’t do well during a week in which the Euro-zone rescue plans fell apart spectacularly of course, then there would be no hope. The implosion within the Greek government and the subsequent uncertainty over the success of the rescue package—a fairly generous affair—should help keep gold in the forefront, even in ‘risk off’ scenarios. - In the gold market, investor interest rose by 1.25 million trozs, with COMEX positions adding 1.40 million. The TOCOM liquidation was partly in connection with the drop in the JPY as the Bank of Japan intervened aggressively in the FX market. This was a healthy increase and represents almost 3 million tozs restored after the late August flush. ### **Gold Exchange Investment, April 09—November 11** 40 2,000 Gold price, $/oz

- NYMEX platinum positions dropped grew by 51,000 tozs over the week, handsomely reversing the midOctober liquidation. ||||||| |**Date**|**ZKB**|**ETFS (UK)**|**ETFS (US)**|**Julius Baer**|**Other**|**Total**|| |**28-Oct-11**|416,499|485,584|710,055|125,793|153,696|**1,891,626**|| |**04-Nov-11**|409,289|491,627|709,638|131,843|151,195|**1,893,592**|| |**Change**|**-7,209**|**6,043**|**-417**|**6,050**|**-2,500**|**1,966**|| - The week ending the 28th October ended with a pronounced dragonfly doji pattern, which gave warning of a reversal in the short term trend—mentioned during last Monday’s report. That chart signal proved good to its word and Palladium dropped to a low of $624 dollars basis December futures on NYMEX. Since then the market has digested decent US auto sales and a generally buoyant

precious complex, and we made a weekly high of $674.50. The price is however constrained by some pressure from two directions for investors. One is the long term support that we saw at $695 levels. That may now work as resistance. Secondly, we are bumping up against the daily Ichimoku cloud. Overall however, the metals performance looks capable of an assault on the important $695 level assuming we do not get another wave of ‘risk off’ activity. - Investors added to longs and appeared to see some short covering as well during the week to the 1st of November, possibly on the large dip. - The ETFs were as good as flat during the week with only a shuffling of positions between the different funds being of note. Please note that I (NF) made an error on the ETFS (US) last week and overstated the metal held in the ETF by around 20,000 Tozs.
